newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $68 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $68 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Monday were slow at mostly $68.00 per cwt, unchanged from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 2,500 head traded at $68.00 in Kansas, mostly slaughter heifers, according to USDA and private sources.
About 100 head of heifers traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma Panhandle at $69.00 in the North Plains, but the market was too light to test, USDA said.
Feedlots reported light inquiry from buyers as the market tried to restart from last week's holiday shcedule, market sources said.

Feedlot cattle prices this week were expected to be supported by continued light supplies of choice cattle and ideas that some meatpackers were short on live inventory for later in the week, the market sources said.
Beef activity was light near midday amid nearly unchanged prices, according to USDA.
